title: Kundalini asleep at the root
hookLine: the bones you sit on, and a serpent asleep across the door of a road
carry: kundalini: the goddess's power, asleep in every body
tomorrow: two students look into the same water. why does only one go back?

lines: A ROAD STARTS AT THE BASE.
SOMEONE IS ASLEEP ACROSS ITS DOOR.
cards: Sit on a hard floor for a minute and you feel it fast: the bones you sit on, the weight going down, the ground pushing back. The Hatha Yoga Pradipika, a Sanskrit manual of yoga, starts its road right there, at the base.
And at the base, someone is asleep. A serpent, coiled, her body lying across the mouth of a road. While she sleeps, the road stays shut.

teach.h: THE ROAD UP THE CENTER: SUSHUMNA.
teach.b: The road is the sushumna, the channel the yoga texts place up the center of the spine. The sleeper is kundalini, the coiled one.

teach.h: AS THE SERPENT KING HOLDS UP THE EARTH.
teach.b: The Hatha Yoga Pradipika opens its teaching on her with a picture from the old stories: as the king of serpents holds up the whole earth, its mountains and forests, so kundalini holds up every practice of yoga.
And here's the big teaching, said plainly. In the Shakta tantras, kundalini isn't a mood or a burst of energy.

teach.h: KUNDALINI: THE GODDESS, ASLEEP IN YOU.
teach.b: She is Shakti, the Goddess herself, the power that makes the world, coiled and asleep at the base of every human body. So the climb isn't self-improvement. It's the Goddess waking in you.
Before she goes anywhere, the map gives the base its own lotus.
The Sat-Cakra-Nirupana calls it Muladhara, the root support, and links it with earth. A map well-known for rising begins with what's underneath you.
And because she's the Goddess, the texts treat her with reverence: practices learned from a teacher, step by step, beginning with how to sit and how to breathe, never rushed.
That's why a 'wake her fast' video makes a grandmother laugh.
You don't hurry a goddess. An X-ray won't show a serpent, and the text never asks it to. It shows where to begin, and who's waiting there.

how: In Shakta and hatha yoga lineages, kundalini is revered as Shakti, the Goddess, and work with her is taught gradually and under a teacher, beginning with posture and breath; the root center, Muladhara, is pictured at the base of the spine.

games.q: what does “the chakras as a map” mean?
o: a ladder of glands from the hips to the head
a row of lights that all switch on at once
a road for attention that starts at the base

games.q: the first page of the map — tap the pairs.
p: the road up the center of the spine
the Goddess's power, coiled at the base
the root lotus, linked with earth

s: the yoga texts treat waking kundalini as a quick trick
the Hatha Yoga Pradipika gives it as practice, learned step by step from a teacher.
in Shakta teaching, kundalini is the Goddess herself, asleep in the body
she's Shakti, the power that makes the world, coiled at the base of the spine.
the map's first station is at the top of the head
it starts at the base, Muladhara, the root, linked with earth.

games.q: a friend sees an ad: 'wake your kundalini in 7 days.' she wants to buy it. by today's lesson, what's the honest answer?
o: she's revered as the Goddess, woken slowly with a teacher, starting from the base.
go for it: kundalini is just energy, so faster is better.
it's only a cute story, so there's nothing there to wake.
games.why: the Hatha Yoga Pradipika treats her practices as guarded and gradual, learned from a teacher; in Shakta teaching she is the Goddess, not a hack.

practice: Sit on the floor or on a firm chair, and feel the bones you sit on press down and the ground press back. Let your spine rise from that base, tall but not stiff, like a road leaving solid ground.
If you pray, greet the Goddess there at the root; if not, stay with the weight and the rising together for the whole sit.

wordCard.voice: The chakras as a map: a road that starts at the base, where the Goddess, as kundalini, sleeps across its door.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the coiled one; the power pictured as a serpent asleep at the base of the spine.

carryVoice: Keep this one: kundalini, the Goddess's power, asleep in every body. The map starts on the ground. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Hatha Yoga Pradipika, chapter 3 (kundali as the support of all yoga practices, as the lord of serpents supports the earth; asleep, she closes the mouth of the sushumna; woken by practice, she rises)
Sat-Cakra-Nirupana (kundalini as the Goddess coiled at the base; the Muladhara lotus, associated with earth)
